# Reactive Complexity & Design {background-color="#e0f2fe"}

## The Challenge of Large Shiny Apps {.compact-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
### Why Modularize?
- Shiny apps are highly interactive, but large apps can become complicated and frustrating to debug.
- Single apps longer than **500 lines** often suffer from subtle paradoxes caused by reactive elements.
- Modularization breaks code into self-contained components (like functions) to allow piece-by-piece testing and reuse.
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Core References
- **[Mastering Shiny](https://mastering-shiny.org)**: Chapters 19 on [Shiny Modules](https://mastering-shiny.org/scaling-modules.html).
- **[Modularizing Shiny app code](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html)** (RStudio).
:::
:::
:::

- For multi-language comparisons, see R and Python implementations in [Shiny Geyser App](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/).

## Key Repositories Overview {.compact-slide}

Several packages and applications illustrate an evolving design pattern aimed at improving usability, performance, and debuggability:

- **[geyser](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/)**: Learning sandbox showcasing R & Python module connection patterns and Shinylive demos.
- **[foundrShiny](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/foundrShiny/)**: Multi-portal package driven by collaborator layout requirements.
- **[qtl2shiny](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/qtl2shiny/)**: Multi-module app for local genomic analysis.
- **[helperApps](https://github.com/byandell/helperApps)**: General-purpose modules designed for direct reuse in other Shiny apps.
- **[shiny_module](https://github.com/byandell/shiny_module)**: Sandbox for testing early reactivity concepts.

# Case Study: geyser {background-color="#e0f2fe"}

## geyser: Modular Concepts {.compact-slide}

Uses the standard Old Faithful geyser app to illustrate module composition, multi-language support, and WebAssembly deployment:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Published Site & Demos
- **[geyser Site](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/)**: Documentation, developer guides, and slide decks.
- **[Shinylive Demos](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/docs/demos/)**: Interactive browser execution without a server.
- **Dual Support**: Modules built for both R and Python (`shiny.express` & `shiny.ui`).
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Modular Progression
- **1. Old Faithful Monolith**: Single-file app.
- **2. UI & Server Split**: Function modularization.
- **3. Single Module**: Server/UI module encapsulation.
- **4. Connected Modules**: Modules over pages, grid rows/cols, twin reuse, and nested app layouts.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
See the [R Shiny Modules Slide Deck](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/docs/geyserShinyR.html) and [Python Shiny Modules Slide Deck](https://byandell.github.io/geyser/docs/geyserShinyPython.html) for detailed walkthroughs.
:::

# foundrShiny: Collaborator-Driven Architecture {background-color="#e0f2fe"}

## foundrShiny: Lab Portals {.compact-slide}

Powers active research portals for the Attie Lab founder mouse studies:

::: {.incremental}
- **Study Portals**: [Founder Calcium Study](https://connect.doit.wisc.edu/FounderCalciumStudy/), [Founder Diet Study](https://connect.doit.wisc.edu/FounderDietStudy/), and [Founder Liver Diet Study](https://connect.doit.wisc.edu/FounderLiverDietStudy/).
- **Developer Guide**: [foundrShiny Articles](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/foundrShiny/articles/devel_guide/).
- **Dependency**: Leverages the core analytical package [foundr](https://github.com/AttieLab-Systems-Genetics/foundr).
- **Scale**: Over **30 interconnected modules** implementing standard 5-function patterns (`*Input`, `*UI`, `*Output`, `*Server`, `*App`).
:::

## Parameter Scoping & Hierarchy {.compact-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
### Input Scoping Levels
To prevent code duplication, inputs are scoped at three distinct levels:
1. **`mainPar`**: Shared parameters (e.g. dataset choice, height) globally available.
2. **`panelPar`**: Localized settings for a specific dashboard panel (e.g. strains, sex, facet overlays).
3. **`plotPar`**: Specific options limited to visualization plots.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
### Calling Hierarchy
- **foundr**: mainPar, about, download, entry, contrast, stats, time, trait
  - **contrast**: panelPar, contrastGroup, contrastTime, contrastTable, contrastTrait, timePlot
    - **contrastGroup**: contrastPlot
    - **contrastTrait**: contrastPlot
  - **stats**: panelPar, contrastPlot
  - **time**: panelPar, timePlot, timeTable
  - **trait**: panelPar, corPlot, corTable, traitNames, traitOrder, traitPairs, traitSolos, traitTable
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Reactive Data Flow
Inputs are passed directly into the
[foundr](https://github.com/AttieLab-Systems-Genetics/foundr)
module. The application avoids global variables; instead, static inputs are filtered into small reactive subsets based on user panels.
:::

## Decoupling Reactivity from Analysis {.compact-slide}

A key architectural shift was completely separating data analysis from the reactive Shiny interface.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Legacy Layout
- **Mixed Code**: Early versions (such as the [foundr v1.4 branch](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/foundr/tree/v1.4)) mixed reactivity, analysis calculations, and plotting configurations in single files.
- **Risk**: Hard to debug, poor test coverage, and fragile scaling.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Decoupled Layout
- **Analysis Package ([foundr](https://github.com/AttieLab-Systems-Genetics/foundr))**: Houses clean, non-reactive R code (ggplot structures, mathematical steps).
- **Shiny Package ([foundrShiny](https://github.com/AttieLab-Systems-Genetics/foundrShiny))**: Manages UI wrappers, reactivity, session states, and client connections.
:::
:::

- **Developer Guide**: See [foundrShiny Data Pipeline & Reactivity Guide](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/foundrShiny/articles/devel_guide/data_flow.html).

# qtl2shiny: Scaling & Modernization {background-color="#e0f2fe"}

## qtl2shiny: Local QTL Analytics {.compact-slide}

Designed for local QTL investigations within a 1-4Mb peak region, including LOD scans, SNP association, and mediation:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
### Analysis Panel Architecture
Organized across 6 dedicated analysis panels:
- **`hotspotApp`**: Genome-wide hotspot count scans.
- **`scanApp`**: LOD scans & founder allele effects.
- **`patternApp`**: Strain distribution pattern grouping.
- **`genoApp`**: Genotype probabilities & gene region tracks.
- **`scatterApp`**: Bivariate mediator scatter plots.
- **`mediateApp`**: Candidate gene mediation scans.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
### Modernization Goals
- **`bslib` Dashboards**: Transition older screens from `shinydashboard` to modern, responsive `bslib` tabs.
- **Developer Guide**: [qtl2shiny Articles](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/qtl2shiny/articles/devel_guide/).
- **Unified Downloads**: Integrated `downr` export widgets across panels.
:::
:::

- See the online [qtl2shiny Developer Guide Overview](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/qtl2shiny/articles/devel_guide/index.html).

## Dependencies & Reactive Debugging {.compact-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### qtl2 Package Stack
- [qtl2](https://kbroman.org/qtl2/): Genotyping and mapping calculations.
- [qtl2ggplot2](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/qtl2ggplot2) ⚠️: ggplot2-based plotting extension.
- [qtl2fst](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/qtl2fst): Database storing scans.
- [qtl2pattern](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/qtl2pattern): SNP association patterns.
- [qtl2mediate](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/qtl2mediate) /
[intermediate](https://github.com/byandell-sysgen/intermediate): Mediation calculations.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Sandbox Learning
- **[`shiny_module`](https://github.com/byandell/shiny_module) package**:
  - Sandbox designed to understand core reactivity rules and event sequences.
  - Useful reference for tracing reactive logs and resolving unresponsive inputs.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Developer Guide Reference
Explore the full architecture and module calling trees in the published [qtl2shiny Module Architecture Article](https://byandell-sysgen.github.io/qtl2shiny/articles/devel_guide/module.html).
:::
